skip_reason: Unscored pending the Walkthrough Scheduler Mini-Rubric - multi-stop intake on a 1800-2200 sqft consolidation move that routed to a virtual walkthrough; pricing, clock, estimate and Save Your Ass were correctly never raised.
top_strength: Textbook agenda opener - the one on this week's pair that fully qualifies. Within seconds of the customer saying "it's a little bit complicated move" she framed the whole call: "Let's start with a few questions to get you on the right track. That should take about five to ten minutes of your time then we'll be able to build an accurate code you can depend on sounds good." What we'll do, how long, and a confirmation ask. She then worked a genuinely messy four-stop consolidation (house, storage unit, second house, destination) in order without losing the thread, and mid-call she stopped to read the inventory back: "So, let me make sure that I've got it correctly. The first location, we are only moving twenty boxes, couch grill, dresser, washer and dryer and fridge." That recap habit is exactly right on a multi-stop job and should be the model for the rest of the team.
coaching_note: Slow down on the intake capture - several details went into the file wrong, and on a four-stop move those errors compound straight into a bad estimate. The customer said of the third location "like twenty to 440 boxes" (i.e. twenty to forty) after describing three beds, a kitchen table, a home office and six wardrobe boxes, and she logged "Twenty boxes. Okay." He said "2200 square feet, free story" and "three bedroom" at 407 Santa Clara, and she came back with "And two bedrooms and what's the walk distance from where we can park the truck to on the door?" He also flagged a real access constraint - the storage unit needs an access code and the stairs are "the annoying part" - and she moved past it with "That we be aware of" rather than confirming who provides the code and logging the stair count. On a walkthrough scheduler the intake record is the whole deliverable, so read back every stop the way she read back the first one.
phone_presence_notes: Warm and patient with a complicated caller - used his name ("Thank you Matthew"), opened with "No worries," and apologized properly for the hold ("thank you so much for patiently waiting. I'm sorry for the long wait") - but the middle of the call is a flat question-by-question march with little acknowledgment of what he actually said.
